documents.summary: University-wide teaching and learning guidelines that welcome ethical, transparent AI use and give instructors a menu of expectation categories, from required use to a ban, to state in their syllabi. It also covers responsibilities, equity, privacy, citation, integrity, professional development and an annual review by the University Teaching Council.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say instructors 'should make clear statements in syllabi' and list categories running from 'Require students to use AI' to 'Forbid use of AI', so the decision is handed to instructors and none is set as default; the document only says it 'encourage[s] the ethical and transparent use' in general. I chose delegates over encourage for that reason.

documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) - Guidance on Use
documents.summary: System-level IT guidance on acceptable, privacy-safe and legal use of generative AI by faculty, staff and students, covering data entry, IP, bias, accuracy, disclosure and accessibility. It says it is guidance, not policy, and sets no course-level AI stance.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'This document is not policy but is guidance' and addresses data, IP, bias and accessibility, with no rule about whether students may use AI in coursework; it only says faculty 'should follow local requirements' for required use. With no stance of its own on course AI use, it delegates to institutions and instructors.
